_about: Text for place actions (events/places.json) and more road events (events/road2.json).
landmark.settle: Stay here and go no further
event.talk_grahamstown.body: The market square is full of transport riders, traders and farmers. Everyone has an opinion about the trek.
event.talk_grahamstown.road: Ask a transport rider about the roads north
event.talk_grahamstown.road.done: "The western road by Cradock has towns and stores, but the Karoo past Cradock is dry. The eastern road over the Stormberg is shorter, and cold in winter. Retief's people went east."
event.talk_grahamstown.prices: Ask why everything costs so much
event.talk_grahamstown.prices.done: "The war, man. Half the cattle on the frontier were driven off, and the rest fetch three times what they did. Now the trekkers are buying every wagon and ox they can find."
event.talk_thaba_nchu.body: Around the trekker fires at Thaba Nchu the talk is all of where to go next.
event.talk_thaba_nchu.north: Listen to those who want to go north over the Vaal
event.talk_thaba_nchu.north.done: "The Highveld is open grass and good water. Potgieter has seen the Mooi River country. Now that the Matabele have gone north, there is land for everyone."
event.talk_thaba_nchu.natal: Listen to those who want to go east to Natal
event.talk_thaba_nchu.natal.done: "Retief says Natal is a garden, with a harbour where we can trade with the world. But to get there you must take the wagons down the Drakensberg."
event.settle_thaba_nchu.body: Some families have stayed near Thaba Nchu for months. There is water and grazing, the mission, and neighbours. You could stay too, and go no further. This would end your trek here.
event.settle_thaba_nchu.yes.done: You unyoke the oxen and begin to build. The road north will have to wait for someone else.
event.turn_back_orange.body: The river is the edge of the Colony. Once across it, there is no British law, no stores, and no going back easily. You could still turn back. This would end your trek.
event.turn_back_orange.yes.done: You turn the wagon south again. Some will call it wisdom and some will call it weakness. The family is together, and that is what matters.
event.farms_for_sale.body: At a farm by the road a family is selling up to go north: furniture, tools, and a few oxen, all going cheap. "We cannot take it all," the farmer says.
event.farms_for_sale.buy: Buy three oxen and a spare wheel (about half the town price)
event.farms_for_sale.buy.done: You pay and drive the oxen off. The farmer's wife watches her things go to strangers with a set face.
event.farms_for_sale.talk.done: They are going north with the next party. You wish each other well on the road.
event.empty_farms.body: The farmhouse is empty. The family has gone north, leaving behind a few broken tools, some old iron and a barrel of tallow in the outhouse.
event.empty_farms.take.done: You load the iron and tallow. Someone may have meant to come back for them.
event.empty_farms.leave.done: You leave the place as you found it. The empty house stays in your mind for a long time.
event.stormberg_snow.body: You wake to snow on the wagon tent and on the hills all around. The oxen stand with their backs to the wind, and the road is hidden.
event.stormberg_snow.wait: Wait for it to melt (two days)
event.stormberg_snow.wait.done: It melts at last. Everyone is cold and cross.
event.stormberg_snow.push.ok: {speaker} finds the track under the snow, and the wagon struggles on.
event.stormberg_snow.push.bad: You go on, but the cold gets into everyone, and by evening two of the party are shivering.
event.dust_storm.body: The wind rises until the air is thick with red dust. You cannot see the oxen in front of the wagon.
event.dust_storm.shelter: Stop and shelter behind the wagon
event.dust_storm.shelter.done: By afternoon the wind drops, and you shake the dust out of everything.
event.dust_storm.push.ok: You keep the span moving and come through it.
event.dust_storm.push.lost: In the dust you lose the track and some of the sheep. It takes hours to find your way.
event.jukskei_snaps.body: A jukskei, one of the wooden pins that hold an ox's neck in the yoke, snaps, and the front pair stops.
event.jukskei_snaps.carve.done: {speaker} cuts a straight piece of hard wood and shapes a new jukskei. The span is soon moving again.
event.grass_fire.body: Smoke on the horizon, and then a line of fire running through the dry winter grass toward you, driven by the wind.
event.grass_fire.backburn: Burn a strip of grass in front of you, as the herders know how
event.grass_fire.backburn.ok: The small fire burns a black strip, and the big fire stops at its edge. Clever work.
event.grass_fire.backburn.bad: The fire jumps the strip in places. You save the wagon, but the tent is scorched and some sheep are lost.
event.grass_fire.run: Drive the wagon and herds away from it as fast as you can
event.grass_fire.run.done: You outrun it, but the oxen are exhausted and some sheep are left behind.
event.wild_dogs.body: In the night a pack of wild dogs gets in among the sheep.
event.wild_dogs.drive: Go out with the guns and drive them off
event.wild_dogs.drive.ok: A shot and a lot of shouting send them off before much harm is done.
event.wild_dogs.drive.bad: By the time they are driven off, several sheep are dead.
event.evening_hymns.body: At the evening fire, someone begins a psalm, and others take it up.
event.evening_hymns.join.done: The singing carries across the dark veld. For a while nobody thinks about the road.
event.evening_hymns.rest: Let those who want to sing, sing; the rest sleep
event.evening_hymns.rest.done: You fall asleep to the sound of singing.
event.lessons_on_the_road.body: The children have had no lessons since you left. They are running wild.
event.lessons_on_the_road.teach: Hold lessons at the midday halt, with the Bible and a slate
event.lessons_on_the_road.teach.done: The children grumble, then settle. Reading and sums, in the shade of the wagon.
event.lessons_on_the_road.skip: Let them be; there is enough to do
event.lessons_on_the_road.skip.done: The children go back to their games.
event.servant_family_news.body: {speaker} has heard from a passing wagon that family back in the Colony is ill. "I should be with them," {speaker} says quietly.
event.servant_family_news.go_home: Give a month's wages and let {speaker.him} go home
event.servant_family_news.go_home.done: {speaker} thanks you and walks south with the passing wagon. You will miss the help.
event.servant_family_news.stay: Ask {speaker.him} to stay; you need every hand
event.servant_family_news.stay.sad: {speaker} stays, but it is plain that the heart has gone out of the work.
event.voorloper_shortcut.body: {speaker} points to a gap between two hills. "That way is shorter, if the ground holds."
event.voorloper_shortcut.take.ok: {speaker} was right: the way is good and saves you half a day.
event.voorloper_shortcut.take.bad: The ground is stony, and a wheel takes a beating.
event.voorloper_shortcut.keep.done: {speaker} shrugs and leads the oxen on along the track.
event.missionary_travellers.body: A missionary's wagon comes the other way, bound for one of the stations. The missionary greets you and asks where you are going.
event.missionary_travellers.welcome: Invite them to share your fire
event.missionary_travellers.welcome.done: You talk long into the night: of the peoples of this country, of the trek, and of what may come of it. In the morning they give you some medicine.
event.missionary_travellers.cool.done: You part civilly, but without warmth.
event.basotho_herders.body: Herders from Moshoeshoe's country are watering cattle at a stream. They watch your wagon with interest.
event.basotho_herders.greet: Greet them and ask about the country ahead
event.basotho_herders.greet.done: With signs and a few words of Dutch they tell you where the water is, and warn you of a bad drift.
event.basotho_herders.trade.done: They bring a bag of sorghum and maize for the beads.
event.powder_found_out.body: News travels fast among the wagons: people are saying your family sold gunpowder beyond the frontier. Some of the trekkers are angry.
event.powder_found_out.admit: Admit it and promise it will not happen again
event.powder_found_out.admit.done: Some are angry, but they respect the honesty.
event.powder_found_out.deny.done: Nobody believes you, and now they think you are a liar as well.
event.council_debate.body: In the laager the council argues late into the night: should the trek go north over the Vaal, or east over the mountains to Natal? You have a vote.
event.council_debate.north.done: Your vote goes with those who want the Highveld.
event.council_debate.natal.done: Your vote goes with those who want Natal. Your own wagon, though, is bound for the Mooi River.
event.council_debate.unity: Speak for the trek holding together
event.council_debate.unity.done: You say the families are stronger together than apart. Some agree, and you are thanked for it.
event.widow_wagon.body: A trekker widow and her children sit by a broken wagon. Her people went on ahead, and she has nobody to help her. She looks at your English wagon doubtfully.
event.widow_wagon.mend.done: It takes all day, but her wagon rolls again. She thanks you in Dutch, and word of it will go ahead of you to the laagers.
event.widow_wagon.carry: Give her two of your oxen
event.widow_wagon.carry.done: Her span is short, so you give her two of yours. She will not forget it, and neither will her people.
event.widow_wagon.pass.done: You drive past. She does not look up.
lock.need_parts: Needs a spare wheel, iron, or a smith
event.share_coffee.body: A trekker family camped nearby has had no coffee for weeks. The children are watching your kettle.
event.share_coffee.share.done: There is laughter around their fire that night. "The English neighbours," they call you after that.
event.sick_ox.body: One of the oxen will not eat, and stands with its head down. {speaker} looks worried.
event.sick_ox.rest: Rest a day and let it recover
event.sick_ox.rest.ok: After a day of rest it starts to graze again.
event.sick_ox.rest.bad: Despite the rest, the ox dies.
event.sick_ox.slaughter: Slaughter it for meat before it dies
event.sick_ox.slaughter.done: The meat is cut into strips and dried as biltong.
event.ostrich_eggs.body: The children find an ostrich nest with a clutch of huge eggs in the sand.
event.ostrich_eggs.take.done: One egg makes an omelette for the whole family. The children are delighted.
history.settle_early: Many trekker families did not go straight on. Some waited for months near Thaba Nchu and the Vet River in 1836-37 while their leaders argued about where to go. Ending your trek here is a choice the game offers, not a particular family's story.
history.turn_back: Not every family that set out kept going. This is invented, and how many turned back is not yet checked against a source.
history.farms_for_sale: James Backhouse met a field cornet in 1839 who had bought his farm from a Boer who emigrated, and another man with eight farms who was about to leave. Trekkers often sold farms and goods cheaply. The sale here is invented.
history.empty_farms: Many frontier farms were left empty as families trekked. This farm is invented.
history.stormberg_snow: Snow on the high ground in winter is a reasonable guess, not yet checked. James Backhouse recorded snow lying till midday in Griqua country in June 1839.
history.jukskei: Oxen were yoked in pairs with a wooden yoke (juk) held by wooden pins called jukskeie. The game of jukskei, played in South Africa today, takes its name from them.
history.grass_fire: Grass fires sweep the dry Highveld in winter. Burning a firebreak in front of a fire is an old herders' method. This event is invented.
history.wild_dogs: African wild dogs were common on the plains in the 1830s. This event is invented.
history.evening_hymns: Worship mattered greatly to the trekkers. In October 1837 the first church north of the Orange was built at Kerkspruit near Thaba Nchu. This event is invented.
history.lessons: Trekker children had little schooling on the road, but some families kept up lessons from the Bible. This event is invented.
history.servant_family: Many servants had families of their own back in the Colony. After 1828 Khoikhoi workers were free to leave an employer. This event is invented and told from the servant's side.
history.voorloper: The voorloper, often a boy or a Khoikhoi or formerly enslaved servant, walked ahead leading the front oxen and picking the way. Much of the trek's success rested on them.
history.missionaries: Missionaries were travelling and working in this country: Wesleyans at Thaba Nchu, and French missionaries with the Basotho, two of whom toured the region in 1836. This meeting is invented.
history.basotho: The Basotho were drawn together under Moshoeshoe in the 1820s and 1830s, in the mountains east of the Caledon River. This meeting is invented.
history.powder_law: Selling gunpowder in the lands beyond the frontier was against the Colony's law. Captain Harris wrote in 1836 that doing so risked twelve months' imprisonment. What happens to your family here is invented.
history.council: The trekker leaders argued about where to go: north onto the Highveld, as Potgieter wanted, or east to Natal, as Retief wanted. The vote here is invented.
history.widow_wagon: This event is invented. It gives an English family a way to earn the trekkers' trust.
history.sick_ox: This is a general sickness, not a named disease. Lungsickness, a terrible cattle disease, only reached the Cape in 1853.
history.ostrich_eggs: Ostrich eggs were eaten, and the shells were used to carry water in this region. One egg is about as much as two dozen hen's eggs. This event is invented.
